title: OSHA Process Safety Management standard as hazardous-chemical management rail
summary: OSHA PSM is encoded as a regulatory management rail for highly hazardous chemicals: it defines covered processes and catastrophic-release prevention/minimization requirements. It is not encoded as proof of compliance, coverage completeness, or prevention effectiveness.

place.scope: United States / professional process-safety infrastructure unless otherwise stated

claims.claim: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 states that the PSM section contains requirements for preventing or minimizing consequences of catastrophic releases of toxic, reactive, flammable, or explosive chemicals, and applies to specified threshold quantities and covered flammable gases/liquids.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: OSHA defines catastrophic release as a major uncontrolled emission, fire, or explosion involving one or more highly hazardous chemicals presenting serious danger to employees in the workplace.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: OSHA’s PSM overview frames PSM as a comprehensive management program integrating technologies, procedures, and management practices for hazards associated with highly hazardous chemicals.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

limitations: Does not establish completeness, compliance, adoption, or effectiveness.
coverage has threshold, exemption, jurisdiction, and enforcement limits
does not by itself expose all near misses or actual barrier health
not a substitute for source-specific accident investigation

handling_notes: Infrastructure records describe visibility/correction rails, not proof that accidents are prevented.
Regulatory/program descriptions must be rechecked before policy or compliance use.
